script: Why did my stepmother stop reading my father's will out loud halfway through a sentence? My dad got sick two years ago, and for eighteen months I was the only one who actually showed up. I drove two hours every weekend to sit with him, feed him, and listen to the same stories he forgot he had already told me. My stepmother and her daughter visited twice, both times just long enough for a photo they posted with captions about family strength. When he passed, I paid for half the funeral myself because nobody else offered. Two weeks later we all sat in a lawyer's office for the will reading. My stepmother read it out with a proud little smile, clearly expecting the house and the savings to go to her daughter. She got through the first two paragraphs before her voice just stopped. My father had attached a separate letter to the will, dated three months before he died. It listed every visit, every missed birthday, and every unanswered phone call, with dates. Then it stated that the house, the savings, and his old workshop went entirely to me, the only one who never needed to be asked twice. My stepmother's daughter had already put a deposit on a car, certain her share was coming. She had thirty days to return it before the dealership canceled the loan. Nobody in that office said a word for almost a full minute. And now the question that family avoids asking out loud is the same one I keep coming back to: why did it take a letter from a dying man to make them finally show up?
